claim: The data-type check rejects any T where `type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`. A type that comes from a referenced assembly through a metadata (DLL) reference has no declaring syntax references. So the case the requirement exists for (ProjectA.MyType compiled into a referenced DLL, formatter declared in Project B) gets MsgPack021 and no generated formatter. The annotated class keeps no implementation, and the build fails with CS0535. Only same-compilation types, or types reached through CompilationReference, ever pass this check.

claim: The acceptance criteria say that if T carries MessagePack attributes ([MessagePackObject]/[Key], or [DataContract]/[DataMember]) they are honoured, and that contractless mode applies only when those attributes are absent. With no surrogate, the collector always calls CreateContractlessMembers. That path never inspects T's attributes, so any T is serialized as public read-write members keyed by name. Keys, Order/Name, IgnoreMember and DataContract opt-in membership are all ignored, and members that T excludes are still serialized.

claim: The core scenario is rejected. The data-type guard includes `|| type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`. Any `T` loaded from a compiled referenced assembly (a real metadata reference such as Project A's DLL) has no declaring syntax references. So `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType>` reports MsgPack021 ('only accessible, non-generic, non-abstract classes and structs are supported') and emits no formatter body. The user's class then fails with CS0535. Only `T` declared in source in the same compilation (or reached through an in-memory CompilationReference) works, which contradicts the acceptance criterion 'even when T is declared in a referenced assembly'.

claim: MessagePack attributes on `T` are never honoured. When no surrogate is given, `CreateContractlessMembers` always serializes every public read-write member by name. It ignores `[MessagePackObject]`/`[Key]` int keys and `[IgnoreMember]` (and `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]`/`[IgnoreDataMember]`) declared on `T`. Example: `T` has `[MessagePackObject] class T { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [IgnoreMember] public int B {get;set;} }`. The generated formatter writes a string-keyed map containing both A and B, instead of an int-keyed array containing only A. This violates the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured.'
